targets.authors: Seidel E-M, Habel U, Finkelmeyer A, Schneider F, Gur RC, Derntl B.
targets.title: Implicit and explicit behavioral tendencies in male and female depression.
targets.evidence_quote: Although we do not have previous genetic research to base our hypotheses on, based on clinical experiences, information processing theories in depression and the research by Seidel and colleagues [ 42 ], we expected avoidance of negative (sad, angry) facial expressions in remitted depressed S/L g -carriers who have experienced childhood trauma, as this represents the most vulnerable subgroup.
targets.outcome_quote: In line with Seidel and colleagues [ 42 ], we expected automatic avoidance of angry faces as well. We did not find this, however.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The specific re-tested Seidel finding is automatic avoidance of angry faces, explicitly not found. New sad-face/genetic interaction results are not a successful replication of Seidel’s angry-face effect.

reasoning: Completed new-sample conceptual replication. Seidel is explicitly used to predict the earlier automatic angry-face avoidance result and that result is compared in discussion. General G x E studies and mechanistic neural/self-report avoidance papers provide wider motivation; the paper introduces a novel genotype/trauma/automatic-behavior combination and does not individually re-test each of those background studies. The broad partly-supports-earlier-GxE statement does not settle the Seidel outcome. Publisher metadata verifies title, DOI and all authors; full article and references saved.
